releasesInRange.name: pnpm 12.10.0
releasesInRange.body:
This release adds an experimental `loaded` node linker, lets `pnpm-lock.yaml` record resolution settings, and reads cached registry metadata faster. It also carries several security fixes, including one that stops a dependency version from writing files outside the global virtual store.

### Minor Changes

- Added experimental `nodeLinker: { type: loaded }` installation. Compatible dependencies load directly from the content-addressable store through an automatically registered Node.js loader. `nodeLinker.excluded` selects packages and their dependency trees to install in the global virtual store.

- `lockfile.includeResolutionSettings: true` makes `pnpm-lock.yaml` record `autoDedupe`, `dedupeInjectedDeps`, `dedupePeerDependents` and `linkWorkspacePackages`. Installs then treat a lockfile that records other values as outdated. A lockfile that records `autoDedupe` is reused by later installs on any machine, so `pnpm run` after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` no longer starts another install [#16583](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16583).

### Patch Changes

#### Security

- `pnpm install` now prevents dependency versions with path traversal from writing files outside the global virtual store.

- pnpm now verifies locked config dependencies against their registry before installing them. Config dependencies must come from an npm registry. The lockfile can no longer replace the integrity of a config dependency pinned with `version+integrity`.

- Lockfile verification now checks the tarballs inside a `variations` resolution against the registry. A `name@version` lockfile entry with an empty `variations` resolution is now rejected.

- `pnpm audit signatures` now verifies signatures against the integrity recorded in the lockfile. Packages without a recorded integrity cannot pass signature verification.

- `pnpm install` and `pnpm publish` now reject archive metadata larger than 64 MiB before reading it into memory. Publishing a pre-built tarball also rejects manifests and README files larger than 64 MiB.

- Two URL or local path dependencies no longer share a virtual store directory when one URL has `+`, `#`, `:`, or `?` where the other has `/`. Such dependencies, including git dependencies pinned with `#`, now get a hash suffix on their directory name.

- The warning about an ignored project `.npmrc` registry setting no longer prints the username and password of a URL-scoped key such as `//user:password@registry.example.com/${PATH}/:_authToken`.

#### Installing and resolving dependencies

- `pnpm install` now fails with `ERR_PNPM_UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL` when a dependency uses a specifier with a protocol pnpm does not support, such as Yarn's `patch:`. On Windows, such a specifier failed with `os error 123`. On other platforms, pnpm linked it to a directory that does not exist. Reading a `package.json` that fails now names the file [#16590](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16590).

- `pnpm install` now fails with `ERR_PNPM_PACKAGE_MANIFEST_INVALI
…(truncated)

releasesInRange.name: pnpm 11.28.5
releasesInRange.body:
This release reads cached registry metadata faster and makes `pnpm config get --global` ignore project settings. It also carries several security fixes for package archives, git dependencies, and config dependencies.

### Patch Changes

#### Security

* pnpm now verifies locked config dependencies against their registry before installing them. Config dependencies must come from an npm registry. The lockfile can no longer replace the integrity of a config dependency pinned with `version+integrity`.

* Lockfile verification now checks the tarballs inside a `variations` resolution against the registry. A `name@version` lockfile entry with an empty `variations` resolution is now rejected.

* `pnpm audit signatures` now verifies signatures against the integrity recorded in the lockfile. Packages without a recorded integrity cannot pass signature verification.

* pnpm now rejects a git dependency whose lockfile repository is empty, begins with `-`, or contains a null byte. Git can no longer read such a value as a command-line option [pnpm/tasks#84](https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/84).

* A git dependency with a `#path:` subpath can no longer reach files outside the repository through a symlink in the subpath.

* `pnpm pack`, `pnpm publish`, and installs of git and local directory dependencies now leave out files that a directory symlink or a `bundleDependencies` entry points to outside the package directory [pnpm/tasks#83](https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/83) [pnpm/tasks#93](https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/93).

* `pnpm deploy` with `deployAllFiles` now rejects symlinks that point outside the package directory. Local package installs with this setting apply the same check.

* pnpm no longer hangs on a package archive with a negative PAX record length or an entry of 4 GiB or more [pnpm/tasks#78](https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/78) [pnpm/tasks#79](https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/79).

* Large package downloads and large files inside gzip and bzip2 package archives now use bounded memory during installation. Package manifests and archive metadata larger than 64 MiB are rejected. `pnpm publish` also rejects manifests and README files larger than 64 MiB in pre-built tarballs before reading them into memory.

* Two URL or local path dependencies no longer share a virtual store directory when one URL has `+`, `#`, `:`, or `?` where the other has `/`. Such dependencies, including git dependencies pinned with `#`, now get a hash suffix on their directory name.

* `pnpm licenses` now removes terminal control characters from package metadata in table output.

* The warnings about ignored project `.npmrc` registry and auth settings no longer print the username and password of a URL-scoped key such as `//user:password@registry.example.com/:_authToken`.

#### Installing and resolving dependencies

* Dependency resolution reads cached registry metadata faster. The metadata cache moved to `<cache-dir>/v12/`, so the first install after upgrading

releasesInRange.name: pnpm 12.10.1
releasesInRange.body:
This release fixes `pnpm install` failures after an `overrides` change and on a filtered frozen install with `catalogPrune`. It also fixes several bugs in the experimental `nodeLinker.type: loaded`, which now keeps its generated files in `node_modules`.

### Patch Changes

- With `nodeLinker.type: loaded`, pnpm now writes its generated files to `node_modules`, which projects already ignore in git. The store manifest and loader are `node_modules/.pnpm/.store-manifest.json` and `node_modules/.pnpm/.store-loader.mjs`. Bin shims are in `node_modules/.bin`.

  Earlier versions wrote `.pnpm-store.json` and `.pnpm-store-loader.mjs` to the project root, and a `.pnpm` directory to the root and to each workspace package. Delete them after reinstalling.

- With `nodeLinker.type: loaded`, packages that ship their own `node_modules` directory, such as `npm` with its bundled dependencies, now load from the store. Before, one such package in the install stopped every Node.js process from starting.

- With `nodeLinker.type: loaded`, scripts can now run a Node.js runtime installed through `devEngines.runtime`. Before, every script that called `node` re-ran its own shim until it failed with "Argument list too long".

- With `nodeLinker.type: loaded`, Node.js processes start faster. In a project with 13,000 stored files, the startup overhead per process dropped from 67 ms to 18 ms.

- `pnpm install` no longer fails with `ERR_PNPM_NO_MATCHING_VERSION` after a change to `overrides` when the lockfile resolves an optional peer dependency to an npm alias of another package [#16654](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16654).

- A frozen install with `catalogPrune` no longer removes catalog entries that `pnpm-lock.yaml` still records. Before, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --filter` failed with `ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_CONFIG_MISMATCH` when some workspace projects were missing from disk [#16638](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16638).

- `pnpm install --fix-lockfile` no longer removes the `deprecated` and `hasBin` fields from lockfile entries [#6600](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/6600).

- With `enableGlobalVirtualStore`, an install that updates `node_modules` now repairs a package in the global virtual store that an interrupted install left without some of its dependency links or package files. Before, such an install kept the incomplete package if the project's `node_modules` already recorded it [#16642](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16642).

- `pnpm install` now skips the Cargo and Python projects inside a nested directory that has its own `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or `.git` directory, such as a git worktree of the same workspace or a separate clone.

- The `Request took` warning for package metadata now starts timing when pnpm sends the request. Before, it also counted the time the request waited for a free request slot, so large installs printed it for requests the registry answered quickly.

prs.title: fix: print devEngines and packageManager warnings on stderr
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

With `devEngines.runtime.onFail: "warn"` (or a `packageManager` / `devEngines.packageManager` mismatch with `onFail: "warn"`), the warning was printed on stdout ahead of the command's own output, breaking `pnpm cache path`, `pnpm list --json`, `pnpm run`, `pnpm exec`, and others whose stdout a script reads.

Both versions had the bug (v11: `cache path`, `run`, `exec`; v12: also every `--json` command). Fixed in both: these pre-command warnings now go to stderr. `--loglevel=error` still hides them. Under `--reporter=ndjson`, v12 still emits them as records; v11 used to drop them (its ndjson sink attaches after the checks) and now prints them on stderr.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16584

## Squash Commit Body

```text
The runtime and package manager checks run before the command and
warned through the command's reporter, which writes to stdout. A command
whose stdout is a value a script reads, such as `pnpm cache path` or
`pnpm list --json`, got the warning prepended to its output.

In v12 the default reporter's pre-command warnings are written to stderr
with the same `[WARN]` label, still gated by the log level. The ndjson and
silent reporters are unchanged. In v11 the same warnings are printed with
`formatWarn` to stderr, unless the log level or the silent reporter hides
them. They bypass the v11 reporter because its ndjson sink attaches after
these checks and used to drop them.

Closes https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16584
```

prs.title: feat: record resolution settings in the lockfile
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Alternative to pnpm/pnpm#16588 for pnpm/pnpm#16583. Both stay open until one is chosen.

pnpm/pnpm#16588 records in the workspace state that an install ran frozen. This PR instead records in the lockfile the settings that shape a resolution, so any machine can tell how the lockfile was produced.

**The setting.** `lockfile.includeResolutionSettings` (opt-in, default `false`). `lockfile` now also takes a section, the way `sideEffectsCache` does:

```yaml
lockfile:
  includeResolutionSettings: true
```

When it is on, `pnpm-lock.yaml` records four settings under their current names:

```yaml
settings:
  autoDedupe: true
  autoInstallPeers: true
  dedupeInjectedDeps: true
  dedupePeerDependents: true
  excludeLinksFromLockfile: false
  linkWorkspacePackages: false
```

Keys in `settings` are written in alphabetical order. The keys pnpm already wrote were in that order, so lockfiles without the opt-in are unchanged.

**Why these four.** A throwaway probe confirmed that `dedupeInjectedDeps`, `dedupePeerDependents` and `linkWorkspacePackages` each change the lockfile a fresh resolution writes. Flipping any of them on an installed project still left the lockfile untouched. `resolvePeersFromWorkspaceRoot` was inconclusive (no difference in my fixture), so it is not included.

**What changes when it is on:**
- **Freshness.** A lockfile that records other values is outdated. `pnpm install` re-resolves it, and `--frozen-lockfile` fails with `ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_CONFIG_MISMATCH
…(truncated)

prs.title: fix: report an unsupported protocol in a dependency specifier
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Makes the failure from pnpm/pnpm#16590 actionable.

`@yarnpkg/core@4.9.2` depends on `got` through a Yarn-only `patch:got@npm%3A11.8.2#~/.yarn/patches/...` specifier. The specifier contains a `/`, so both stacks' local resolvers claim it as a path. Before this PR:
- On Linux and macOS, both stacks warned and linked `got` to a directory that does not exist.
- On Windows, pnpm v12 failed with a bare `os error 123`. Rust maps `ERROR_INVALID_NAME` to `ErrorKind::InvalidFilename`, so the missing-directory fallback never ran.

npm rejects the same specifier with `EUNSUPPORTEDPROTOCOL: Unsupported URL Type "patch:"`.

Changes:
- **Unsupported protocol (v11 and v12):** when the local resolver finds that a specifier it claimed by path shape names a missing directory, and the specifier opens with a `<scheme>:` of two or more characters, it now fails with `ERR_PNPM_UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL`. The error names the protocol and the specifier, and its hint points to `overrides`. I checked the hint against the issue's reproduction: overriding `got: ^11.8.2` resolves `got@11.8.6`.
  - The check runs only on the missing-directory branch, so a successful resolution does no extra work. An existing directory whose path looks like a protocol (`scheme:pkg/dir`) still resolves.

feat(install): add loaded linker with GVS exclusions
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds experimental `nodeLinker: { type: loaded }` installation to pnpm v12. Enable it in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, optionally list package names in `nodeLinker.excluded`, and use normal install, run, and exec commands. Compatible packages load directly from verified content-addressable store blobs. Selected packages and their complete dependency trees use ordinary global virtual store entries, with their existing graph identities and dependency links.

pnpm generates the runtime manifest, embeds and writes the standalone loader, creates JavaScript executable shims, and preloads the loader for scripts and child processes. Store pruning preserves live CAS blobs and materialized GVS trees. Patched packages materialize automatically; packages requiring builds must be selected explicitly, and normal build approval still applies. The default application layout has state and bins under `.pnpm/` and creates no application node_modules.

Node.js 26.10.0 or later is required. This is opt-in and experimental: direct filesystem access and independent tool resolvers can still require additional materialization or resolver integration. Existing node_modules directories must be removed when switching modes. CAS repeat installs regenerate the runtime manifest; the optimistic installation shortcut is disabled. No static analyzer is included.

prs.title: fix(pull-requests): check the fork remote before a continued rebase pushes
prs.author: snmsoodan
prs.body:
`resolve-pr-conflicts.sh --continue` resumes a rebase that the script paused. It stays on the detached HEAD instead of running `gh pr checkout`, and it verifies that the paused rebase is rewriting the head branch of the PR named on the command line, so a stale PR number cannot push one PR's rebase onto another PR's branch.

The push target was still taken on trust. The script chooses the remote named after the head owner and force-pushes there:

```sh
git remote get-url "$HEAD_OWNER" &>/dev/null && REMOTE="$HEAD_OWNER" || (add it)
git push "$REMOTE" HEAD:"$HEAD_BRANCH" --force-with-lease
```

That name is created by `gh pr checkout`, which `--continue` never runs, and `git remote add` fails loudly while `git remote get-url` succeeds on any remote that already holds the name. Three ways for the name to point elsewhere:

- **the fork was renamed**, so `<old owner>` is someone else's repository, or the fork now lives at another repository name;
- **an unrelated remote already holds the name** (a second fork, a hand-added remote);
- **the branch check passes but the remote does not** — the two are independent, and only the branch check existed.

The result is a force-push of the rewritten commits into a repository that is not the PR's fork.

## Changes

- Read the head repository from the PR itself (`headRepository.nameWithOwner`) instead of assuming `<head owner>/pnpm`, and use it for the auto-added remote URL. A renamed fork is no longer looked for, or added, under the wrong re
…(truncated)

prs.title: fix(package-manager): validate version and enforce slot containment in global virtual store
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes GHSA-jg5c-8mvg-5wph: *pnpm v12 global-virtual-store escape: dependency manifest version path traversal writes files outside the store*.

In pnpm v12 with `enableGlobalVirtualStore: true`, dependency slot directories are laid out under `<store_dir>/v3/slots/<name>/<version>/...`. If a dependency's package manifest specifies a malicious version containing path traversal components (e.g. `../../escaped` in tarball or git dependencies), slot directory resolution escaped the virtual store and wrote files outside the store directory.

This change:
- Adds `is_valid_package_version` in `pnpm_package_name` to reject empty versions, `.`, and traversal sequences (`..`, `/`, `\`).
- Validates package versions when constructing slot paths and lockfile entries, rejecting traversal versions.
- Enforces virtual store slot containment in `validate_virtual_store_slot_containment` and `SlotPaths::create` before creating slot directories.
- Validates slot containment during fresh lockfile installation (`install_with_fresh_lockfile`) immediately after slot layout.

This vulnerability affects only pnpm v12. pnpm v11 uses a project-local virtual store (`node_modules/.pnpm`) with different directory layout and resolution mechanics.

prs.title: fix(loaded): preserve frozen-store installs and prune unused GVS entries
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes two edge cases in the newly merged loaded linker (https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/16482).

When `storeDir` is a non-hidden directory inside the project, `pnpm store prune` could crawl the store itself and keep unused GVS slots alive. The project scan and dependency walker now exclude the canonical store root, while preserving roots referenced by the loaded manifest. The regression covers both `store` and `node_modules/store` inside the project.

Loaded installs with `frozenStore: true` now skip project registration writes. Writable loaded stores still require successful registration to protect their files from pruning. The loader documentation explains retention for externally managed frozen stores.

Validation: 24 scoped Rust tests passed, covering store pruning and the loaded CLI. The new regressions verify that a non-hidden local store loses unused GVS trees, retains live roots, and permits frozen installation when the store registry cannot be written. The original feature's full 14,570-test Rust run passed before merge. CI passed on `1e6c9482ff816eece2d1cdc597a87e328b09589b`: Rust tests on Linux, macOS, and Windows, all lints, WebContainers, and benchmark checks. All 52 completed checks passed (7 skipped). Required push hooks also passed. CodeRabbit approved this head with no actionable comments. Qodo found no bugs; its Windows-coverage suggestion is answered with passing Windows job evidence in https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/16600#issuecomment-5994

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16598.

prs.title: fix(run): accept ECMAScript regex syntax in script selectors
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

`pnpm run "/<regex>/"` compiled the selector with Rust's `regex` crate, which has no lookaround or backreferences. A pattern such as `/^hello:(?!b).*$/` failed to compile, fell back to being read as a literal script name, and the run failed with `ERR_PNPM_NO_SCRIPT`. pnpm v11 uses a JavaScript `RegExp`, so the same command worked there.

This switches the selector to [`regress`](https://crates.io/crates/regress), an ECMAScript regex engine, so the syntax and semantics match v11. Script names are matched as UTF-16 code units, as an unflagged JavaScript `RegExp` does, so `/^.$/` does not match a name made of one astral character. The `regex` crate is still used elsewhere in the CLI.

v11 is not affected, so this is a v12-only fix.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16604

## Squash Commit Body

```text
`pnpm run "/<regex>/"` compiled the pattern with the `regex` crate,
which has no lookaround or backreferences. A selector such as
`/^hello:(?!b).*$/` failed to compile, fell back to being read as a
plain script name, and the run failed with ERR_PNPM_NO_SCRIPT. pnpm v11
uses JavaScript's RegExp, so the same command worked there.

Compile the selector with `regress`, an ECMAScript regex engine, so the
pattern syntax and semantics match v11. Match over UTF-16 code units
through regress's UCS-2 input, since an unflagged JavaScript RegExp
treats a surrogate pair as two characters.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16604
```

- [x] I checked the referenced issue and verified that none of the

prs.title: fix(cafs): validate PAX header lengths and avoid 32-bit integer truncation
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

In `pnpm11/store/cafs/src/parseTarball.ts`:
- Validate that parsed PAX record lengths are strictly positive and within the remaining buffer bounds, and verify the presence of the space delimiter.
- In `paddingOf`, compute block padding using modulo arithmetic instead of 32-bit bitwise operators to prevent signed integer truncation on large archives or records with sizes >= 4 GiB.
- In `parsePaxSize`, verify that size is a safe integer.

Fixes https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/78
Fixes https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/79

## Squash Commit Body

```text
fix(cafs): validate PAX header lengths and avoid 32-bit integer truncation

In the tarball parser, validate that parsed PAX record lengths are
strictly positive and within the remaining buffer bounds, and verify
the presence of the space delimiter. In paddingOf, calculate block
padding using modulo arithmetic instead of 32-bit bitwise operators to
```
